key_insight: A frozen vision foundation model can outperform specialized EEG foundation models when EEG signals are rendered as task-optimized images.
engineering_relevance: SeeEEG offers a parameter-efficient way to reuse pretrained vision encoders for EEG tasks by learning the signal display rather than updating the backbone.
method: Render each EEG channel in a dedicated patch row as a fixed-gain waveform or frequency-scaled scalogram.
Optimize montage, filtering, and contrast through the frozen backbone using at most 1,113 trainable parameters per view.
Evaluate frozen encoders with identical readout heads and transfer learned displays to V-JEPA 2.1 without further display optimization.
evidence_signal: Across eight datasets, DINOv3-based SeeEEG beat seven EEG foundation models in balanced accuracy on every dataset; replacing DINOv3 with a random ViT-B reduced scores by 15.2 points on average.
watch_item: The results establish frozen-encoder performance, not superiority over fine-tuned EEG models, and display optimization still requires task supervision.
paper_title: Your Vision Foundation Model Is Secretly an EEG Foundation Model
